public_rationale: The retrieved disclosures do not establish the claimed AI losses. Microsoft reports substantial AI-attributed revenue growth, while Amazon reports profitable AWS operations. Neither measure establishes AI-specific profitability. Large investment budgets also cannot be treated as current losses. With no matched revenue-and-cost evidence for the six companies and no specified accounting basis, the claim cannot fairly be supported or contradicted.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The big tech companies make little money from AI and lose billions of dollars on it.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft, Meta, Google, Apple, Amazon and Tesla aren't making much money from AI — in fact, they're losing billions of dollars on whatever revenues they do make from it.
statement.document_title: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

from_speaker: Microsoft, Meta, Google, Apple, Amazon and Tesla
aren't making much money from AI
losing billions of dollars on whatever revenues they do make from it
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that the named companies' AI activities generate substantial losses after attributable costs, rather than merely requiring substantial investment.
The context concerns generative AI. Profits from older advertising or recommendation systems cannot automatically settle the claim.
Use the latest generally reported quarter before publication: the quarter ending in March 2025. Apple's corresponding fiscal quarter ended March 29.
The wording does not establish whether billions refers to each company, their combined losses or an annual pace. Check company-specific results and aggregation without silently annualizing.
No accounting basis is stated or identified in the supplied passage.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable AI-specific revenues and attributable expenses establish multibillion-dollar losses on the stated scope, with the individual-versus-combined interpretation made explicit.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable AI-specific financial results establish material profits or otherwise exclude the claimed multibillion-dollar losses on the same scope and period.

evidence.locator: Amy Hood's prepared remarks, Intelligent Cloud results
evidence.explanation: Microsoft reports a material AI contribution to cloud revenue growth. This is revenue attribution, not a disclosure of AI profit or loss.
AWS was profitable as a whole. Its mixed AI and non-AI business cannot establish whether Amazon's AI activities made profits or multibillion-dollar losses.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable AI-specific income statements or transparent cost-allocation estimates for the relevant quarter, plus clarification of the accounting basis and whether the loss threshold applies individually or collectively.
